jobs.title: Global Public Policy Manager, Compute, Infrastructure & Sovereign AI

reading.body:
Three open AI policy and governance roles are listed, two of them posted in September 2026 and one in October 2026, across Cohere, ServiceNow, and Trusteq. That is the entire sample. No conclusion about hiring volume, trend, or direction can be drawn from three postings.

The titles are the useful part. Cohere's role names compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI directly, which places policy work next to the physical buildout rather than beside it. ServiceNow's is a FinOps governance lead, tying cost control of AI spend to the same function. Trusteq's is a consulting position in Munich. Two of the three sit at companies that buy or operate compute at scale, and the third sells advice about it.

What this does not cover is the market. The listed sources include federal, aggregated, remote, and European boards, but only three postings survived into this set, so the absence of other employers is not evidence they are not hiring. There is no salary, seniority distribution, or time series here. Read the titles as a signal about how policy work is being framed, not as a measure of how much of it exists.

The three titles split into two kinds of work that are usually filed together. Cohere's role is external: policy toward governments, sovereign compute, and infrastructure. ServiceNow's is internal: FinOps governance, meaning control of what the company itself spends on AI. Both are labeled AI Policy and Governance, but one faces outward and one faces inward, and the data gives no way to tell how often that pairing occurs elsewhere.

Geography is the other split the titles carry. Two roles are United States, one explicitly remote, and the third is Munich. The European listing comes from Arbeitnow, the European source in the set, and the two US listings come from Ashby and SmartRecruiters, which are company career boards. That is consistent with the source list, but with three postings it is a coincidence as easily as a pattern.

The dates are worth reading precisely. Two postings are September 2026 and one is October 2026, and the page was built on October 3, 2026. So the October posting is at most three days old and the September ones are roughly a month old. All three were live at build time, which means this is a snapshot of open roles, not a record of hiring over time.

What does an AI governance role actually do, based on these titles?

The titles point to two distinct jobs. Cohere's names compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI, which is policy work aimed at governments and the physical buildout. ServiceNow's names FinOps, which is cost governance of AI spend inside a company. Trusteq's is a consulting position, so the work is advisory rather than in-house.

Is there any salary data here?

No. The data contains no salary, compensation, or pay range for any of the three postings.

How many of these roles are remote?

One of the three is marked remote, the Cohere role, which is listed as United States. The other two carry no remote flag.

Which companies are hiring for this function?

Cohere, ServiceNow, and Trusteq. Those are the only three employers in the set, and each appears once.

Does this show whether AI governance hiring is growing or shrinking?

It cannot. Three postings with no prior period to compare against give no trend, and the page states no time series. The only timing information is that two were posted in September 2026 and one in October 2026.

Why are there so few listings when the source list includes federal, aggregated, and remote boards?

The data does not say. The sources are listed as the boards the page draws from, but only three postings are present, and nothing here explains the gap between the source list and the count.
